Subject: Greenfield Health — private deployment privacy debrief & required artifacts

Hi Harriet — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we can align on the Private (VPC) deployment path and PII handling requirements. Great to meet the security and infra folks.

Summary from our side:
- Deployment mode: Private (VPC) with customer-managed peering (no public ingress).
- Data types: patient identifiers + clinical notes (PII + PHI). Greenfield will mark which fields are considered sensitive; we requested a data map.
- Retention: Greenfield requires 6 months of raw request logs and 90 days of full-text audit logs; retained in your KMS-backed S3 in us-east-1.
- Logging controls: redact token-level content for responses that include PHI; archive request/response headers for traceability.
- Egress policy: deny all outbound traffic except to approved internal IP ranges and the designated ops jump host. Air-gap approach preferred for PROD scope if on-prem components are used.

Action items (owners & ETA):
1) Harriet / Greenfield: share the data classification spreadsheet and a network diagram showing VPC subnets, NAT, and jump-host (ETA: Wed 10/7) — item: Greenfield_Network_Diagram.pdf (you mentioned this on the call).
2) Soojin: produce a minimal acceptance checklist for Private deployment (PII handling, retention TTLs, logging knobs, failover) and an initial SOW appendix sketch (ETA: Thu 10/8).
3) Ben: review quantization and cache policies that preserve auditability (Ben will propose config guards) — ETA: Thu 10/8.
4) Marissa: coordinate procurement and give a ballpark for Dedicated vs Private cost delta for the projected Q4 volume — ETA: Fri 10/9.

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Will Greenfield allow any outbound telemetry to Redwood-managed endpoints for aggregated metrics? If not, we’ll provide a zero-telemetry deployment option (requires additional ops runbook).
- Is there an internal retention policy that supersedes the 6-month request-log requirement?
- For air-gapped / on-prem components: can Greenfield provide a maintenance window for kernel and inference-engine updates?

Please confirm document drop location (Drive link preferred) and we'll pick this up as soon as we have the network diagram + data map. If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag inline.

Thanks — good next steps.

—

Thanks Soojin — this looks right. Attaching our network diagram and a first-pass PII data map extract. Note: the data map is redacted for certain fields (client confidentiality) but should be enough for scoping.

A few clarifications from our infra/security side:
- Telemetry: we can allow only aggregated, non-PII metrics to a Redwood endpoint over an outbound TLS connection. No raw request/response payloads may leave the VPC.
- Retention: internal policy is 12 months for audit logs; for this project we can negotiate to 6 months if Redwood retains only header-level metadata and stores payloads in our KMS-protected bucket.
- Air-gap: PROD model updates must be scheduled in a maintenance window; we can support quarterly kernel rollforward with a pre-approved package.

See attachments: Greenfield_Network_Diagram.pdf (application/pdf), PII_Data_Map_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

This is good. I can take point on the config proposal. Initial notes:
- We'll propose a tenant-scoped KV cache with a 0s persistence policy for any text labeled PHI, and a separate persistent cache for embeddings (non-PII only).
- Suggest an option flag: "redwood.telemetry.mode = minimal" that disables outbound telemetry entirely; alternate: allow aggregate metrics over TLS to the provided endpoint (per Harriet).
- For retention: provide a tiered policy in the SOW appendix: (a) 90d detailed audit logs in Greenfield S3; (b) 12mo header-only logs retained; (c) on-request purge workflow tied to Greenfield's lifecycle API.

Will draft and share by EOD Thu 10/8. If Greenfield confirms quarterly maintenance windows for air-gapped updates, that will simplify our ops checklist.
